question:
Using linear approximation, answer the following:

(a) Obtain the linear approximation of $f(x)=\sqrt{x}$ near $x=25$.

(b) Hence, find an approximate value of $\sqrt{25.3}$.

(c) Determine the approximate percentage change in the value of $\sqrt{x}$ when $x$ changes from $25$ to $25.3$.
explanation:
(a)
For $f(x)=\sqrt{x}$,
$$f'(x)=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}$$
At $x=25$,
$$f(25)=5\quad\text{and}\quad f'(25)=\frac{1}{10}$$
The linear approximation near $x=25$ is
$$L(x)=f(25)+f'(25)(x-25)$$
Therefore,
$$L(x)=5+\frac{x-25}{10}$$

(b)
For $x=25.3$, the change in $x$ is
$$dx=25.3-25=0.3$$
Using the linear approximation,
$$\sqrt{25.3}\approx 5+\frac{0.3}{10}$$
$$\sqrt{25.3}\approx 5.03$$

(c)
The approximate change in $f$ is
$$df=f'(25)\,dx=\frac{1}{10}(0.3)=0.03$$
The approximate percentage change is
$$\frac{df}{f(25)}\times 100=\frac{0.03}{5}\times 100$$
$$=0.6\%$$
